South Korea completes Arctic-Europe commercial voyage, eyes regular service despite risks

South Korean President President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority, and officials hope to launch regular services by 2030.

The PanStar Acro, South Korea's first such commercial voyage to Europe via the Arctic, make its way to the port of Felixstowe, in Felixstowe, Britain on Sep 11, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Chris Radburn)

SEOUL: A South Korean container ship completed the country's first commercial round trip to Europe via the Arctic on Sunday (Oct 11), as authorities bank on the route helping turn the port of Busan into a global maritime hub. The PanStar Acro docked in the southeastern port 50 days after setting sail on Aug 22. Authorities say the Arctic route could cut typical voyage times by around a third. President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority, and officials hope to launch regular services by 2030. But the project risks friction with Western allies hoping to keep Russia isolated during its war in Ukraine. The route runs along Russia's Arctic coast, and Seoul consulted with Moscow about the journey, including whether the ship needed help to tackle any problems, such as getting stuck in ice. On its outbound voyage, the vessel passed through Arctic waters and reached its first European port, Felixstowe in Britain, before calling at Rotterdam and Gdansk and returning home via the Arctic. The trial voyage also highlighted the challenges ahead. Before the departure, PanStar told Reuters it was seeking about 1,300 twenty-foot equivalent units of cargo, but the ship left with 737 TEU of cargo plus empty containers. Industry experts have said the route's value will depend on reliable schedules, the costs of slowing to avoid ice, special insurance premiums and extra fuel use.

KATHMANDU: Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday (Oct 11) to move to safer places after a massive flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties. A dry landslide in Chumnubri village in Gorkha district, about 100km west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said. The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing. "We have asked villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat.

Oct 11 : Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson and Tim Seifert will return to New Zealand's one-day international (ODI) squad for next month's home series against India, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Sunday. Neither batter Allen nor fast bowler Ferguson have played a 50-over match for New Zealand since 2023, while Seifert's last ODI outing came in 2025. All-rounder Rachin Ravindra, who dislocated his right shoulder during a promotional shoot last month, returns to the squad after he was ruled out of the Twenty20 series beginning on October 22. "We're incredibly lucky to have the depth that we do to have 21 players involved in the series," head coach Rob Walter said in a statement.

New Zealand, who host India in five T20s, five ODIs and two tests, have named two separate squads for the first three ODIs and the final two matches. Seven additional players will join the squad after the third ODI in Hamilton on November 10, with a portion of the group departing to begin preparations for the test series. "With the ODI World Cup just one year away it's important for us to also view these matches as valuable preparation for that event," Walter added. GENEVA: The World Health Organization (WHO) said on Saturday (Oct 10) that it still does not know what caused the pneumonia that killed a Russian lab worker at an anti-plague research centre in Siberia this month, and that no case of plague had been registered. The WHO said the Russian state regulator reported that tests of the lab worker and those who came in contact with her were negative for the high-threat pathogens tested, that her contacts still showed no symptoms, and that no further linked cases of severe pneumonia had been identified. "Based on the information provided ... (the) WHO has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission associated with this event. A key uncertainty remains the absence of a confirmed diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker," it said in a statement. The lab worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Oct 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and causing public health fears on social media. Global health officials have been extra alert to fatal pneumonia cases of undetermined cause since the COVID-19 pandemic, which began with a cluster of fast-spreading fatal respiratory illness in China. The cause of individual pneumonia cases can often not be determined. Russian authorities have said the lab worker was appropriately vaccinated and that they found no microorganisms linked to her work in her body. On Thursday, Russia said it had completed health checks on all the worker's contacts. It says it had provided full information to the WHO according to established procedures.

Oct 11 : Real Madrid's Vinicius Jr has apologised to his teammates and the club's fans after being sent off in the 1-0 win over Villarreal in LaLiga at the Santiago Bernabeu on Saturday. Vinicius now faces a nervous wait for the ruling of the disciplinary committee, which could see him miss Real's fixture with rivals Barcelona on October 25 at Camp Nou. The Brazilian thought he had scored Real's second goal but his effort was disallowed after a VAR review found he should be dismissed for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up. After the match, Vinicius, who came on in the 52nd minute and was red carded 20 minutes later, posted on social media, saying, "sorry to the team and the fans."

Oct 10 : US women's coach Emma Hayes shook off a dismal 2-0 defeat on Saturday in the first of two friendlies against Spain, with the Americans building towards next month's World Cup qualifiers. The match between top-ranked Spain and the Olympic champions was billed as a marquee showdown but the visitors took control as Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro scored inside 15 minutes.  Spain's Adriana Nanclares saved a second-half penalty from Lily Yohannes to keep a clean sheet for the world champions. "When you play the best team in the world you have to execute everything really well in the first instance," said Hayes. "Did I think we did enough to score a goal? Of course we did. Did we do enough to score more than one? Absolutely.

"We just didn't make necessarily the right decision and execute with the quality I know we should have." The US had 10 shots on target to three from Spain, who had Athenea Del Castillo sent off in added time for pulling Michelle Cooper's hair three minutes after coming off the bench.  Hayes said that efficiency would be a key target for the US when the two sides play again on Tuesday.  "We create the most chances in world football. But finishing, we do not do that in world football," Hayes told reporters. "So I wasn't concerned about us creating today, and I'm not concerned about us finishing. You just have to lock in, get the details right, and keep working on it." The US aim to qualify for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil via the Concacaf W Championship, three years after their worst performance at the global tournament where they exited in the last 16 and Spain staked their territory as the world's finest. Briton Hayes' arrival months later from Chelsea sparked a renaissance for the US, who collected gold in Paris and welcomed back veteran Mallory Swanson to camp this month. "We've got some really, really good players and we're a really good team regardless of the result today," said Hayes. "I think we're much closer to them than we were three years ago."

NAPLES, Italy, Oct 10 : Inter Milan maintained their strong start to the Serie A campaign with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Parma on Saturday, while two goals from Kevin De Bruyne eased Napoli to a 3-0 home win against Frosinone following the international break. First-half goals from Petar Sucic, Hakan Calhanoglu, who converted a penalty, and Marcus Thuram put the champions firmly in control inside the opening 31 minutes. The result lifted leaders Inter to 16 points from six matches. “After a three-week break, we didn’t know how things would go. We’ve worked well during this period, the players have trained well. I’m happy,” Inter head coach Cristian Chivu told DAZN. The defeat marked a difficult first game in charge for Parma coach Alberto Gilardino, who succeeded Carlos Cuesta following his departure in late September.

“I think you always have to be clear-headed at different moments of the game, depending on who you’re playing against and what you’re up against. The overall picture tonight is that Parma started well, but when you are naive, you pay the price,” Gilardino said. MCTOMINAY RETURNS FOR NAPOLI In Naples, Scott McTominay was named among the substitutes after recovering from a heart problem as Napoli overcame a sluggish start to beat Frosinone. Napoli were awarded a penalty in the 29th minute and after Rasmus Hojlund's spot kick was saved by Lorenzo Palmisani, the effort was ordered to be retaken as the goalkeeper was ruled to have moved off his line. Kevin De Bruyne converted the second attempt before Noa Lang doubled Napoli's lead three minutes later. McTominay made his return just after the hour mark to a standing ovation from the home crowd, although he was unable to influence the contest. De Bruyne wrapped up the victory late on, finishing from close range for his second goal of the evening. The win provided a much needed boost to Napoli as they had suffered two defeats and a draw in their previous five matches. They moved to sixth place with 10 points. "We had to win," De Bruyne told Sky. "It's a very difficult schedule, but we have to move forward and do our best." Second placed AS Roma and Lazio, who are both on 13 points, will be in action on Sunday. Roma visit Como, while Lazio host Monza. Surprise package Cagliari, fourth on 12 points, face a tough home test against Juventus on Sunday.

Source: Reuters

Oct 10 : Paris St Germain's Maghnes Akliouche scored his first goal for the club as the champions eased to a 3-1 home victory over Le Mans in Ligue 1 on Saturday, while league leaders AS Monaco were held to a frustrating 2-2 draw by visiting Toulouse. The game was played in a tense atmosphere as, amid student protests across France, a banner was unfurled at the stadium which read: "Your riot police repress, our youth resists." Scuffles broke out as police tried to remove the banner and eventually the entire stand was temporarily emptied of spectators. PSG took the lead with a penalty converted by Lucas Beraldo, but Le Mans levelled in the second half through Louis Mafouta who blasted home for his fourth Ligue 1 goal this season.

Home coach Luis Enrique reacted by making four substitutions at once just before the hour mark and one of those, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, fired them ahead two minutes after coming on as he reacted quickest to a rebound. Akliouche then ended the game as a contest with the third, his first goal since switching from Monaco at the start of the season. PSG were awarded a penalty in added time but Desire Doue’s effort was saved by goalkeeper Nicolas Kocik. The win leaves PSG in fifth on 11 points after six games. Monaco let a 2-0 first-half lead slip as they were held by Toulouse. They have 14 points and a one-point lead over Lille. Edan Diop scored their opener and then turned provider for Matthis Abline to net his first Monaco goal since a move from Nantes. Casper Tengstedt pulled one back for the visitors with a penalty just after the break before teenager Sion Oppong netted his first Toulouse goal to make it 2-2. Lille briefly moved top as they won 1-0 at home to 10-man Le Havre before being leapfrogged later on by Monaco. Dilane Bakwa scored the winner in the fifth minute but Lille were run close by Le Havre, who lost Ayumu Seko to a red card for a professional foul just past the hour mark. Paris FC remain fourth despite a 1-0 loss at Lorient and sit above local rivals PSG on goal difference. They had more of the ball but Lorient took their chance as Gabin Bernardeau netted after 68 minutes. Brest scored four first-half goals before eventually running out 5-1 victors over 10-man Angers in a one-sided contest. Ludovic Ajorque, Lucas Tousart, Kenny Lala, Mama Balde and Pathe Mboup scored for Brest, while Prosper Peter netted a consolation for the visitors, who had Jordan Lefort sent off after 59 minutes.

Source: Reuters
